stories.headline: Pevkur declares confidence in US defense commitment during Vilnius visit, warns Europe not ready to face Russia alone
stories.summary: Estonian Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur, speaking to Reuters during an official visit to Vilnius on April 16–17, stated Estonia has no doubt the United States would come to its defense if Russia attacked, while warning that European allies are not yet capable of replacing US military support. He also called for NATO to help resolve the Iran conflict to allow US attention to shift back toward Ukraine, and met with Lithuanian counterpart Robertas Kaunas to discuss defence cooperation ahead of the NATO Ankara summit.

stories.headline: President Karis and Defence Minister Pevkur conduct state visit to Lithuania, focusing on security and Rail Baltica
stories.summary: President Alar Karis made an official state visit to Lithuania on April 15–16, accompanied by Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur and parliamentary delegates. Activities included a state dinner with President Nausėda, Karis receiving an honorary doctorate from Vytautas Magnus University, a joint press conference addressing NATO cohesion and Russian threats, visits to Ukrainian refugee centers by first lady Sirje Karis, and inspection of the Rukla military base.

stories.headline: President Karis publicly criticizes Foreign Ministry capacity, triggering political dispute with Tsahkna and debate over presidential re-election
stories.summary: President Alar Karis sparked a public dispute by stating in an interview that the Foreign Ministry lacks the capacity to think beyond the immediate crisis, without the people, skills or sometimes knowledge to take a long-term view. Foreign Minister Tsahkna and PM Michal pushed back sharply, accusing Karis of overstepping. The row escalated into a broader debate about the role of the presidency, Karis's prospects for a second term, and a heated radio debate between Tsahkna and Isamaa leader Reinsalu who accused each other of 'Orbánism.'

stories.headline: Baltic states bar Slovak PM Fico from using airspace for Moscow Victory Day parade trip
stories.summary: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania all denied permission for Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico's aircraft to transit their airspace for a planned visit to Moscow's May 9 Victory Day parade. Foreign Minister Tsahkna confirmed the denial, stating Estonia will not allow its airspace to be used for travel to Russia while Russia continues aggression against Ukraine. The ban is a repeat of the same decision made the previous year.

stories.headline: KAPO annual report reveals record spy arrests, warns of growing Chinese influence operations
stories.summary: Estonia's Internal Security Service (KAPO) released its 2025 annual report, revealing a record number of people—16 in total—were detained for cooperating with Russian intelligence agencies. The report also highlighted growing Chinese influence operations targeting Estonian public figures through sponsored trips, and warned about Russia's Eastern Orthodox Church as a vector for influence. The majority of those caught were ordinary citizens without state access.

stories.headline: Estonia opposes EU pay transparency directive; coalition split emerges as Tsahkna reverses earlier position
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Tsahkna announced at a government press conference that Estonia opposes the EU pay transparency directive, calling it 'ideological' and over-regulatory. The announcement drew immediate scrutiny because Tsahkna had personally approved the directive on Estonia's behalf three years earlier. Eesti 200 party leader Kristina Kallas subsequently issued a contradictory statement saying Estonia must adopt the measures that reduce the gender pay gap. A joint government press conference with PM Michal, Tsahkna, and economy minister Keldo covered these and related positions.

stories.headline: EKRE support drops to 11% in spring polls as Isamaa and Centre Party lead ratings
stories.summary: A Turu-uuringud poll showed EKRE's support fell from 15% in January to 11% in April, placing the party fifth. Isamaa led at approximately 24% with Centre Party close behind; the governing Reform Party polled at around 14%, equal to the Social Democrats. Polling data were published by multiple sources including ERR and the polling firm itself.

stories.headline: EKRE leader Helme condemns post-Orbán Hungary election results as democratic backsliding; internal fallout follows
stories.summary: EKRE chairman Martin Helme reacted sharply to Viktor Orbán's electoral defeat in Hungary, calling it a dark day for nationalists and conservatives. In a radio interview he said he would have declared a state of emergency. An opinion piece by Jüri Toomepuu criticized Helme's narrative, and a local EKRE councillor in Viljandi publicly called people to 'take up arms' in a social media post referencing Helme's Hungary commentary, subsequently denying he meant literal violence.

stories.headline: US arms delivery delays to Estonia expected due to Iran war consumption; HIMARS ammunition most affected
stories.summary: Defence Minister Pevkur warned that US military operations in Iran may delay weapon and ammunition deliveries to Estonia, particularly HIMARS rockets and Javelin anti-tank systems. He noted he had scheduled a call with the US defence minister and expressed hope that countries investing heavily in defence like Estonia would get priority. A separate ERR report indicated the delays primarily affect HIMARS ammunition.

stories.headline: Riigikogu cancels planned excise duty increases to cushion energy price impact from Iran conflict
stories.summary: The Estonian parliament passed legislation cancelling planned increases to excise duties on alcohol, tobacco, fuel and electricity that had been scheduled for 1 May. Finance committee chair Annely Akkermann stated the purpose was to offset the impact of rising energy prices stemming from the Middle East conflict. The bill passed its second and final readings during the week.
